definitions.explanation: The distinctive taste and aroma of food or drink, often implying a subtle, refined, or characteristic quality. More nuanced than {味|あじ}, suggesting the overall sensory impression including both taste and smell.

examples.japanese: バター{風味|ふうみ}のクッキーを{焼|や}いた。
このチーズは{独特|どくとく}の{風味|ふうみ}がある。
examples.english: This cheese has a distinctive flavor.

examples.japanese: {長時間|ちょうじかん}{煮込|にこ}むことで、{素材|そざい}の{風味|ふうみ}が{引|ひ}き{出|だ}されて{深|ふか}い{味|あじ}わいになる。
examples.english: By simmering for a long time, the flavor of the ingredients is drawn out, creating a deep taste.

notes:
USAGE:
{風味|ふうみ} refers to the combined taste-and-aroma profile of food, suggesting a more refined or nuanced quality than {味|あじ} alone. It is also commonly used as a suffix meaning "-flavored": バター{風味|ふうみ}, しょうゆ{風味|ふうみ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風味|ふうみ}が{良|よ}い (good flavor/aroma)
- {風味|ふうみ}を{生|い}かす (to bring out the flavor)
- {風味|ふうみ}が{落|お}ちる (the flavor deteriorates)
- {風味|ふうみ}{豊|ゆた}かな (rich in flavor)
- 〜{風味|ふうみ} (-flavored: バター{風味|ふうみ}, ガーリック{風味|ふうみ})

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {風味|ふうみ}: flavor (combined taste and aroma; refined quality)
- {味|あじ}: taste (direct taste sensation; broader usage)
- {香|かお}り: aroma, fragrance (smell specifically)
- {味|あじ}わい: savoring, appreciation of taste (literary/poetic)
